## 1 Overview

Market area analysis (Trade Area Analysis) defines and studies the geographical area from which a business draws its customers. The Huff Model is a classic probabilistic geospatial model used to predict the probability that a consumer from a specific origin (e.g., a village) will patronize a particular store, based on store attractiveness (such as size or sales) and travel distance/impedance relative to competitors.

This exercise assumes the role of a data analyst within the business development team of a fast-food franchise. The objective is to delineate the trade areas of existing stores in Taichung City and produce corresponding spatial maps to support market analysis and strategic decision-making.

### 1.1 The Data

Four data sets are used in this exercise:

Geospatial data:

`STORES_TN`: Store locations data in ESRI shapefile format.

`VILLAGE_TN`: Village boundary data in ESRI shapefile format.

Aspatial data:

`pop2019.csv`: Population data of Taichung City in 2019 (H_CNT, P_CNT, M_CNT, and F_CNT indicate household count, total population, male population, and female population respectively).

`Store_sales_data.csv`: Store sales transaction data.

## 2. Getting Started

Install and launch the necessary R packages into the RStudio environment:

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, MCI, tmap, ggstatsplot)
```

## 3. Importing Data

### 3.1 Importing Geospatial Data

Use *st_read()* from the sf package to import the three geospatial layers into R.

```{r}
stores <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                  layer = "STORES_TC")
```

```{r}
town <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                layer = "TOWN_TC")
```

```{r}
village <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                   layer = "VILLAGE_TC")
```

All data sets were checked to ensure that they share the same projected coordinate system (TWD97 / TM2 zone 121 / EPSG: 3826).

Inspect the boundaries interactively using tmap:

```{r}
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(town) + 
  tm_polygons() + 
  tm_shape(village) + 
  tm_polygons() + 
  tm_shape(stores) + 
  tm_dots()
tmap_mode("plot")
```

```{r}
tmap_mode('plot')
```

### 3.2 Importing Aspatial Data

Import the aspatial datasets using read_csv() from readr:

```{r}
pop2019 <- read_csv("data/aspatial/pop2019.csv")
```

```{r}
store_sales <- read_csv("data/aspatial/Store_sales_data.csv")
```

```{r}
summary(store_sales)
```

## 4. Data Preparation

### 4.1 Aggregating Store Sales

Aggregate store sales data by Store Code:

```{r}
store_sales_aggre <- store_sales %>%
  group_by(`Store Code`) %>%
  summarise(
    "Total_Bill" = sum(Bills, na.rm = TRUE),
    "Total_Sales" = sum(Amount, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### 4.2 Relational Join & Store Size Assignment

Append the aggregated sales data onto the stores spatial data frame and assign a proxy metric for store attractiveness (Store_size).

```{r}
stores <- stores %>%
  left_join(store_sales_aggre, 
            by = join_by(Store_CD == `Store Code`)) %>%
  mutate(Store_size = 1)
```

```{r}
summary(stores)
```

### 4.3 Tidying Population Data (pop2019)

Check the village ID structures to ensure compatibility before joining:

```{r}
glimpse(pop2019)
```

```{r}
glimpse(village)
```

Remove the hyphen (-) from pop2019 village IDs to match the VILLCODE format in the village spatial file:

```{r}
pop2019 <- pop2019 %>%
  mutate(V_ID = str_remove_all(V_ID, "-"))
```

```{r}
village <- village %>%
  left_join(pop2019, by = join_by(VILLCODE == V_ID))
```

### 4.4 Checking for Missing or Zero Values

```{r}
summary(village)
```

Filter out records containing missing population attributes:

```{r}
village <- village %>%
  filter(!is.na(P_CNT))
```

```{r}
any(is.na(village$H_CNT))
any(is.na(village$P_CNT))
any(is.na(village$M_CNT))
any(is.na(village$F_CNT))
```

## 5. Computing Distance Matrix

Calculate the surface centroid of each village polygon, then compute the pairwise distance matrix between village centroids and store locations.

```{r}
village_center <- st_point_on_surface(village)
distmat <- st_distance(village_center, stores)
```

```{r}
rownames(distmat) <- village$VILLCODE
colnames(distmat) <- stores$Store_CD

distmat_long <- distmat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "VILLCODE") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -VILLCODE,
    names_to = "Store_CD",
    values_to = "distance"
  ) %>%
  mutate(distance = as.numeric(distance))
```

## 6. Preparing Interaction Matrix

Build the interaction matrix required by the MCI package:

```{r}
interaction_matrix <- distmat_long %>%
  left_join(
    stores %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      select(Store_CD, Store_size),
    by = "Store_CD"
  ) %>%
  relocate(distance, .after = last_col())
```

```{r}
summary(interaction_matrix)
```

## 7. Computing Huff Model

```{r}
huff_share <- huff.shares(
  interaction_matrix, 
  "VILLCODE", 
  "Store_CD", 
  "Store_size", 
  "distance"
)
```

### 7.1 Trade Area Analysis for a Single Store

Select market share data for a specific store (e.g., Store_CD == "BT"):

```{r}
market_share <- huff_share %>%
  filter(Store_CD == "BT")
```

```{r}
Trade_area <- village %>%
  left_join(market_share)
```

```{r}
selected_store <- stores %>%
  filter(Store_CD == "BT") 
```

```{r}
tm_shape(Trade_area) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "p_ij",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
      style = "quantile", 
      n = 10, 
      values = "brewer.blues"
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Patronage Probability")
  ) +
  tm_shape(selected_store) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3, fill = "red", col = "black") +
  tm_title("Distribution of Patronage Probability of Store BT by village") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_borders(fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

### 7.2 Store Sales Analysis and Validation

Estimate store sales by multiplying patronage probabilities by village population:

```{r}
huff_share_pp <- huff_share %>%
  left_join(
    village %>% 
      st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      select(VILLCODE, P_CNT),
    by = "VILLCODE"
  ) %>%
  relocate(distance, .after = last_col())
```

```{r}
huff_total <- shares.total(
  huff_share_pp, "VILLCODE", "Store_CD",
  "p_ij", "P_CNT")
```

```{r}
store_sales_est <- stores %>%
  left_join(huff_total,
            by = join_by(
              "Store_CD" == "suppliers_single"))
```

```{r}
store_sales_nongeom <- store_sales_est %>% 
  st_drop_geometry()

ggscatterstats(
  store_sales_nongeom,
  x = sum_E_j,
  y = Total_Sales)
```

The final code chunk reshapes the long-format interaction probabilities into a wide-format table with villages as rows and stores as columns. 

```{r}
huff_share_wider <- huff_share %>%
  select(VILLCODE, Store_CD, p_ij) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Store_CD, 
                values_from = p_ij)
```

Code chunk below will be used to tidy the village sf data frame.

```{r}
village_tidied <- village %>%
  select(VILLCODE, H_CNT, P_CNT) %>%
    mutate(HH_SIZE = P_CNT/H_CNT) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()
```

Code chunk is to do a comparison of the probability values across the stores, picking out the highest value and returning the `Store_CD` in the new column `TA`.

```{r}
huff_TA <- huff_share_wider %>%
  mutate(
    TA = names(pick(2:29))[
      max.col(pick(2:29),
              ties.method = "first")
    ]
  )
```

Next, we will select only `VILLCODE` and `TA` from `huff_TA`, and join it with `village` to create `village_TA`. 

```{r}
huff_TA_tidied <- huff_TA %>%
  select(VILLCODE,TA)

village_TA <- village %>%
  left_join(huff_TA_tidied,
            by = join_by(VILLCODE))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 12
tm_shape(village_TA,) + 
  tm_polygons(fill = "TA") +
  tm_title("Trade Areas of Stores") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_borders(fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```
